issues.description: Bitmap24::set parameter identifiers are inconsistent between the header declaration and the implementation, which is confusing for students. In the header (Bitmap24.hpp) the method is declared as: void set(int i_x, int i_y, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b); whereas the definition in Bitmap24.cpp is: void Bitmap24::set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b) { ... } (the implementation treats the first parameter as the row/y index and the second as the column/x index). Call sites in main.cpp use bitmap.set(i, j, ...) where i is the row and j is the column, which matches the implementation but contradicts the header parameter names. This mismatch between the API declaration and the implementation's parameter naming/documentation is likely to confuse students about the intended meaning and order of the first two integer parameters (x vs y).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the parameter identifiers and their documented meaning consistent between declaration and definition. Two reasonable options: (A) Update the header declaration to match the implementation and call sites (first parameter = row/y, second = column/x): void set(int i_y, int i_x, char i_r, char i_g, char i_b); and add a short comment clarifying 'first parameter is row (y), second is column (x)'. OR (B) Update the implementation and all call sites to use (int i_x, int i_y, ...) consistently if you prefer (x,y) ordering. Prefer keeping implementation and call sites intact and changing the header/documentation to avoid breaking existing usage.
